title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Sharing the Relationship Bonus Across a Customer's Accounts
content:
The relationship bonus on Savings & Money Market Accounts belongs to the customer's whole savings relationship rather than to any one account. This page explains when it is earned at all and how one balance ceiling is shared out among several accounts of the same owner.

## Rule

**Qualifying checking.** On any given day the bonus is earned only if, when that day begins, the customer holds a Personal Checking account in active status whose tier appears among the qualifying checking tiers of the savings account concerned. The bank's checking records for the same customer are the evidence.

**Daily ordering.** Every day, the end-of-day balances of the customer's savings accounts that are active or dormant are lined up from largest to smallest; where two balances are equal, the account opened earlier goes ahead.

**Sharing the ceiling.** Working down that line, only the balances eligible for the bonus are accumulated into a running combined total. An account's balance earns the bonus only up to the point where that running combined total reaches the balance ceiling of the account's own tier; whatever part of the balance lies past that point earns no bonus.

**Accounts outside the sharing.** An account on a tier with no qualifying checking tier, or on a tier whose bonus rate is 0.00, is not part of the sharing at all and uses up none of anyone's ceiling.

**Crediting.** The bonus is paid when the statement cycle closes, as a separate interest credit identified as the relationship bonus component.

Which checking tiers qualify, the bonus rate and the ceiling are all taken from the savings account's own tier.

## Illustration (hypothetical balances and ceilings)

Both accounts below are assumed to qualify for the bonus. The ceilings are invented for the example and are not tier figures.

| Order | Account | End-of-day balance | Running total after this account | Ceiling assumed for its tier | Balance earning the bonus |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | Account A | 40000.00 | 40000.00 | 150000.00 | all 40000.00 |
| 2nd | Account B | 30000.00 | 70000.00 | 60000.00 | 20000.00, the part that brings the running total up to 60000.00; the other 10000.00 earns nothing |

Had Account A held 65000.00 instead, the running total would already have passed Account B's assumed ceiling when Account B was reached, and none of Account B's balance would earn the bonus that day.

## Points of judgement

**Is the checking test made at cycle close?** No. It is made day by day, as each day starts.

**Does the balance of an account whose tier pays no relationship bonus shrink the room left for the others?** No. Such an account stays outside the sharing and is not added to the running total.

**Two accounts end the day at the same balance. Which goes ahead?** The one with the earlier opening date.
